title: 1.5.37 Settle It in the Console
description: Two expressions, one pair of brackets, and a question answered in four seconds. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Predict, then log the first expression
steps.instructions: Write your prediction in a comment, then log 2 + 2 * 3.

steps.title: Say what the difference tells you
steps.instructions: In a comment, state the rule the two answers demonstrate.

steps.title: Settle one more of your own
steps.instructions: Log any other expression you were unsure about: a comparison, a string method, a typeof. The point is the habit, not the answer.

requirements.title: Logs 2 + 2 * 3
requirements.description: Prints the un-bracketed expression. Help: 1.2.7 (Arithmetic Operators and Type Coercion)

requirements.title: Logs (2 + 2) * 3
requirements.description: Prints the bracketed expression. Help: 1.2.7 (Arithmetic Operators and Type Coercion)

requirements.title: The rule is stated in a comment
requirements.description: A comment naming precedence, order of operations, or that multiplication happens first. Help: 1.2.7 (Arithmetic Operators and Type Coercion)

requirements.title: A third expression of your own
requirements.description: At least three console.log calls, so something beyond the two given was checked. Help: 1.2.7 (Arithmetic Operators and Type Coercion)

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote JavaScript for the lab "1.5.37 Settle It in the Console". The task they were given: Write your prediction in a comment, then log 2 + 2 * 3. You cannot run their code: read it and judge what it WOULD do. Judge each criterion by whether the idea is achieved, however the student wrote it. Different variable and function names, template strings, arrow functions, semicolons, spacing, quotes and order are all fine. Do not require any particular structure unless the criterion names one. Mark a criterion missing only when the idea is absent or the code does the opposite. Code inside a comment never runs. Write each note for THIS student's own code: in a not-met note, name the exact line or name in their code that causes the problem (quote at most a few words of it), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected code. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their code satisfied it. Do not use generic praise.
